plant.culled_by: TWO INDEPENDENT EYES. Rafe, device walk, 2026-09-06; and round 30's blind seat, 2026-09-06.
plant.verbatim: flat pale block, no interior texture (seat) / too shiny on worn areas, character washed out (Rafe)

seat.BEST_WHY:
The light survives the exposure. In the rectangle around the figure (x300–470, y455–540) the floor reaches a mean luma of 166 with **zero pixels above 245** — nothing clips — and the mortar grid keeps the same normalised local contrast under full illumination (0.051) as it has out in the gloom. You can trace an unbroken horizontal joint running right through the hottest part of the frame, three tiles left of the figure and three tiles right of it. That is the hard part of a carried-light scene and it is the part that's done.

Underneath it, the presentation is clean: a 2× nearest-neighbour upscale at consistent odd-row phase (95.3% row-pair identity across the interior), so every pixel is the same size and nothing is resampled to mush. The crack network reads as damage rather than decoration — the long crack entering at x≈235, y≈480 runs diagonally, then **turns and travels along a mortar joint** for about two tiles near y≈565 before breaking off again, which is what a crack in laid stone actually does. And the upper wall band at y≈425–445 has driven pins and horizontal timber with joints at irregular intervals — that's the repair-with-salvage brief actually landing in the geometry, not in a caption.
seat.WORST_WHY:
Two things a person sees before they see anything else.

First, **the barrels are cut in half by the floor.** Both barrels at y≈190–217 terminate on a perfectly straight horizontal line at y=217, exactly where the grey cobble row begins. Their stave lines are still faintly visible continuing *down over the stone*, so the sprite is being drawn and the cobble tile is compositing on top of it. That's a draw-order bug, shipped.

Second, **they are the same barrel twice.** I sampled the pixel column at x=125 and x=173 down through both sprites — identical RGB at every single row. Mean absolute difference across the whole 26×22 sprite: 1.2, and that residual is the dirt speckle showing through. Same lid ellipse, same bung dash on the right, same stave spacing, 48px apart. The two chests at top-left are the same trick vertically.

Beyond those: the water is an **axis-aligned rectangle**. Dirt at x=248, teal at x=249, hard step, no bank, no shoreline, no transition tile, no darkening at the edge — for 380 pixels straight down. The dirt/cobble border is the same untreated rectangle. And each chest is two projections glued together: a flat top-down lid welded to a front-elevation plank face, with a hard seam between them, sitting on a floor drawn straight from above.

flip_list: **Every fire in this frame subtracts light.** I compared identical regions against 2 (global exposure matched within 1 luma across four control patches). Floor left of the firepit: −9.5. Floor right of it: −10.7. Floor below it: −13.8. Floor around the burning stick pile: −15.8. There is a lit flame in a ring of hearthstones at (596, 548) and the stones of its own ring are darker than the bare floor was before the fire was placed there. Make each fire prop a light emitter: warm falloff of 2–3 tiles, brightest on the hearthstones themselves, and remove the darkening halo the placement pass is currently applying.

The lantern at (330–360, 535–570) is illegible at play size. Its left edge has a hard outline, its right edge has none — the pixels just stop into the floor. Close the silhouette on all four sides with the same outline weight, and give the top face a distinct value so it reads as an object seen from above rather than a front panel.
That lantern and the firepit ring are drawn in near-elevation — you see a front face and a grate — inside a strictly overhead frame. Redraw both to the same camera as the floor.

The same two-crossed-sticks motif appears three times inside four tiles: dark brown at (275, 612), saturated red-orange at (405, 612), and as a parallel pair at (530, 618). Cut it to one, and vary the remaining timber by length and angle rather than by hue.

The crossed sticks at (405, 612) sample (158, 49, 20) — a saturated red that appears nowhere else in the set, on stone that samples (127, 93, 64). Bring the props onto the environment ramp; they currently read as a different artist's layer dropped on top.
None of the five floor props has a contact shadow. They sit on the stone with no anchor. Add a one-to-two-pixel occlusion darkening on the side facing away from the carried light.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
item_exit.item: #202 - the top-to-face turn: the worn arris, built in the traffic-modulated form WALL-RECIPE.md 4.1 said was the only adoptable one
item_exit.claim: face and top read as separate objects because the only thing at the turn is a dark line, and a dark line separates. The bar draws a pale worn edge there. It was refused as a UNIFORM band and is adoptable modulated by traffic, which the face family's four-step age index now supplies

DELIVERED, worst cell reported: lit wall cap 75.83 -> arris 113.33, ratio 1.495; DIM WALL cap 25.58 -> arris 44.20, ratio 1.728 - over the bar's band, and the 6.3 exposure, stated for the gate. Zero blown pixels in either (0 of 532, 0 of 300), so 183's 'never blown' holds. The turn now profiles cap 75.8 -> arris 113.3 -> shadowed underside 25.0 -> face 59.0 where it was 75.8 -> 24.8 -> 59.0.

law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
